## What the two misses mean

`reversed_relation` and `inflated_strength` are invisible to these rules by construction. Reversing an edge leaves the same two variables in the same passage with the same verbatim span, so all four rules still pass; inflating a strength label changes nothing any rule reads. **This is the clearest argument in the project for the semantic verifier**: roughly two fifths of the corruption families, and the two that a careless graph is most likely to contain, cannot be caught by matching text at all.

It also bounds the claim in the other direction. The three families the rules do catch are caught deterministically, cheaply and with no model, so a verifier that spends budget re-checking citations is spending it in the wrong place.

## Reading the numbers

Per-type counts are **uneven by construction** (D-21): the gold set supplies 19 seeds but only 9 hedged links, so `inflated_strength` has a denominator of 9. Quote every rate with its denominator; a macro average over families is not meaningful here.

Corruption detection is sound even though the gold graphs are not yet adjudicated, because each corruption was applied mechanically and is known by construction. **The false-alarm rate is not**: a control is only clean if its gold edge was right, so that figure inherits whatever adjudication changes.
